explain.text: At 130 words a minute, two minutes holds $130 \times 2 = 260$ words. As a check, 130 a minute is about 2.17 a second, and $2.17 \times 120 \approx 260$. The 45 s result is about 98 words, so pick your two best numbers.

explain.text: A strong answer names one flaw and the check that would find it. Survivorship is the classic flaw in share data: firms that failed drop out, so the past looks better. Backtesting Engine l16 lists it under real data.

screens.prose: A candidate's two-minute account, one sentence a line. An interviewer would stop the candidate twice: once at a missing number, once where the account drifts.

lines: I asked whether 12-month momentum survives trading costs on UK shares.
I used 20 years of monthly prices for about 600 shares.
Each month I bought the top tenth by past return and sold the bottom tenth.
I charged 10 basis points on every trade.
Before costs the Sharpe ratio was 0.9.
After costs it was a lot lower, but still positive.
The 1-month lookback lost money once costs were in.
So costs matter most for fast signals.
I also play chess, which taught me patience.
Next I would test the 12-month rule on held-out years.
I would also let the cost grow with trade size.
The code and a one-page note are linked on my CV.
